_doc: HMTc Category 6 (Seafood) compiler config for the SHARED variants-format engine tools/standards/compile-cat1.mjs (driven via the thin wrapper tools/standards/compile-cat6.mjs) — HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default). Rewritten 2026-08-14 from the prior cells-format (explicit-id) config so that every published cell is selected by an explicit scope regex against data/evidence/regulatory_limits.csv, strictest across jurisdictions. This restores the RICH per_country (all weighed jurisdictions) that the cert 'Source regulations' table renders, which the lean explicit-id lookup had collapsed. Occurrence never selects a number. The six animal-seafood subcats are as-consumed WET weight (ppb) taken at face value (no 8:1 reconstitution); the seaweed subcat is DRY-weight (mg/kg DM) and its numbers must NEVER be numerically compared against the wet-weight fish ppb.
_read_across_canon: tHg on the finfish subcats is a POLICY selection of the EU 2023/915 mercury tier (higher-mercury 1000 for predatory; lower-mercury 300 for non-predatory/freshwater) and canned (general fishery 500), carried as a disclosed government read-across (basis:gov) so the scope-selected general/lower rows do not mis-bind it; shellfish and cephalopod tHg are scope-selected (crustacean/mollusc general 500; cephalopod lower-mercury 300). total Cr = HK Cap 132V fish/crustacean/oyster 1000 (India all-fishery 12000 concurs; cephalopods reach only the India 12000). Ni = EU 2024/1987 seaweed 30000 on seaweed; animal seafood has no Ni ML -> control (not-material). Sn = canned-only migration limit (canned-seafood Mexico 100000; seaweed accumulates organotin -> French CSHPF 5000 DM); non-canned animal seafood -> not-material. Al = no seafood contaminant Al ML anywhere -> control (not-material). MeHg = speciation-bounded by tHg on every subcat -> not-material. Cr-VI = speciation-bounded by total Cr -> not-material. Two CONFIRMED seaweed tightenings bind the French CSHPF edible-seaweed maxima (ANSES 2017-SA-0070 Table 3): Cd 2000->500 (fr_cshpf_seaweed_cd_500) and tHg 2500->100 (fr_cshpf_seaweed_thg_100).
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default; scope-selected strictest across jurisdictions; MeHg speciation-bounded by tHg on animal seafood; seaweed on dry-matter basis)

fish-marine-predatory.name: Marine predatory fish (tuna, swordfish, shark, king mackerel, marlin, billfish)
fish-marine-predatory.scope_note: Marine predatory finfish (tuna, swordfish, shark, king mackerel, marlin, billfish), fresh or frozen, edible portion. Lead binds the muscle-meat-of-fish 200 line; total mercury binds the EU higher-mercury-fish 1000 ceiling (not the general 500). MeHg is bounded by tHg. Total chromium binds HK fish 1000 (India all-fishery 12000 concurs, looser). Ni and Al are screened (no sovereign ML); Sn and Cr-VI are not-material. Canned predatory fish route to the canned-seafood subcategory.

tHg.label: edible portion, wet weight; total mercury. Predatory species (tuna, swordfish, shark, marlin, king mackerel) bind the EU 2023/915 higher-mercury-fish ceiling of 1000; the general 500 does not apply to these listed higher-mercury species.

MeHg.control: Methylmercury is the organomercury speciation of total mercury and is arithmetically bounded by it (MeHg <= tHg). The binding total-mercury ceiling for this subcategory (total mercury ceiling) is equal to or stricter than the lowest applicable sovereign methylmercury ML for this product, so passing the total-mercury limit guarantees methylmercury compliance and no separate methylmercury ceiling is published. Audit-affirmed.
MeHg.reference_method: Total-mercury screen; reflex MeHg speciation is optional and cannot exceed the tHg ceiling.

Ni.control: No jurisdiction sets a nickel maximum level for fish or fishery products anywhere in the register or worldwide (EU 2024/1987 nickel covers plant foods and seaweed only, not animal seafood). Nickel is screened rather than assigned an invented or mis-based number.
Ni.reference_method: Total-nickel screen (ICP-MS); no sovereign fish/fishery Ni ML.

Sn.control: Fresh/frozen seafood has no tinplate contact; inorganic tin is a can-migration analyte. A full register Sn sweep shows every seafood tin ML is canned/tinplate-migration scope; no sovereign sets a non-canned seafood tin matrix limit. Canned product is certified under the canned-seafood subcategory tin limit.
Sn.reference_method: Packaging control (non-tinplate); ICP-MS per-lot screen; escalate to the canned-seafood Sn limit if packaged in tinplate.

Al.control: No credible regulator sets an aluminium contaminant maximum level for seafood in any checked jurisdiction. Aluminium in seafood is background; dietary aluminium is managed by weekly intake against the EFSA/JECFA TWI, not by a per-food maximum level.
Al.reference_method: Total-aluminium screen (ICP-MS); managed by intake vs the EFSA/JECFA TWI; no per-food seafood contaminant ML to align to.

Cr-VI.control: Hexavalent chromium is the Cr(VI) speciation of chromium and is bounded by the total-chromium government limit (Cr-VI <= total Cr), which binds at 1000 for fish here. No jurisdiction sets a Cr-VI food maximum level, and in a reducing animal-tissue matrix Cr(VI) is reduced to Cr(III), so there is no chromate pathway in seafood (unlike lead-chromate-adulterated spices). Rebuttable if a routed source reports hexavalent chromium.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Bounded by the total-chromium government limit; reflex Cr-VI speciation only on anomalously elevated total chromium.

fish-marine-non-predatory.scope_note: Marine non-predatory finfish (sardine, anchovy, salmon, cod, herring, mackerel), fresh or frozen, edible portion. fish-freshwater.scope_note: Freshwater finfish (tilapia, catfish, trout, carp), fresh or frozen, edible portion. Lead binds muscle-meat-of-fish 200; total mercury binds the EU lower-mercury 300 ceiling (conservative subcategory-wide selection). MeHg bounded by tHg; total Cr binds HK fish 1000; Ni/Al screened; Sn/Cr-VI not-material. Canned product routes to the canned-seafood subcategory.

tHg.label: edible portion, wet weight; total mercury. Trout is an EU 2023/915 listed lower-mercury species (300); the freshwater subcategory is held to the 300 ceiling as the consumer-protective bound covering the whole subcategory (tilapia/catfish/carp are not individually EU-listed and would otherwise fall to the general 500 — 300 is the stricter, conservative selection).

shellfish.scope_note: Shellfish (crustaceans — shrimp, crab, lobster; and bivalve molluscs — clams, oysters, mussels), fresh or frozen, not canned. Lead and cadmium bind the stricter crustacean 500 across the whole subcategory; inorganic arsenic binds the EU crabs/prawns/shrimps 100; total mercury binds the crustaceans/molluscs general 500. MeHg bounded by tHg; total Cr binds HK 1000 (crustaceans and oysters; India all-fishery 12000 concurs); Ni/Al screened; Sn/Cr-VI not-material. Cephalopods are certified in their own subcategory; canned shellfish route to the canned-seafood subcategory.

cephalopods.scope_note: Cephalopods (octopus, squid, cuttlefish), fresh or frozen, not canned. Lead binds EU cephalopods 300; cadmium binds EU cephalopods 1000; inorganic arsenic binds the EU cephalopods 50; total mercury binds the EU lower-mercury 300. MeHg bounded by tHg; total Cr binds India all-fishery 12000 (the only on-scope sovereign for molluscan cephalopods; HK regulates fish/crustaceans/oysters, not cephalopods); Ni/Al screened; Sn/Cr-VI not-material. Canned cephalopods route to the canned-seafood subcategory.

canned-seafood.name: Canned seafood (canned tuna, canned fish and other tinplate-packed fishery products)
canned-seafood.native_basis_label: edible portion, as consumed (wet weight); tinplate-packed
canned-seafood.scope_note: Canned/tinplate-packed fishery products (canned tuna, canned fish). Lead binds the tuna/bonito 200; total mercury binds the general fishery 500; inorganic arsenic binds EU fish-other 100. Tin IS material here (canned) and binds Mexico canned-fishery 100000. MeHg bounded by tHg; total Cr binds HK fish 1000; Ni/Al screened; Cr-VI not-material.

seaweed-kelp-foods.name: Seaweed / kelp foods (nori, wakame, kombu, dulse — dried, as sold)
seaweed-kelp-foods.native_basis_label: edible dried seaweed as placed on the market (DRY-WEIGHT basis, mg/kg dry matter) — never numerically compared to the wet-weight animal-seafood ppb
seaweed-kelp-foods.scope_note: Edible dried seaweed/kelp food products (nori, wakame, kombu, dulse) sold as dried, on a DRY-WEIGHT basis (mg/kg DM) — these numbers must never be numerically compared against the wet-weight animal-seafood ppb. Cadmium (500) and total mercury (100) bind the French CSHPF edible-seaweed maxima (confirmed tightenings from 2000 and 2500). Lead 5000 and total arsenic 5000 bind the Israel dried-seaweed lines; inorganic arsenic 1000 binds FSANZ (HK concurs). Nickel binds EU 2024/1987 seaweed 30000; tin binds the French CSHPF seaweed 5000. MeHg and Cr-VI are not-material (speciation-bounded); aluminium and total chromium are screened (no on-scope sovereign ML). Seaweed used as a dietary supplement (>=80% dried seaweed) routes to the supplements category.

MeHg.control: No jurisdiction sets a seaweed methylmercury ML (all sovereign MeHg limits are fish/fishery scope), and seaweed is a marine primary producer into which methylmercury does not biomagnify (it biomagnifies up the food chain, not into algae), so MeHg is a negligible fraction of total mercury and is bounded by the tHg ceiling (tightened to France CSHPF 100 DM).
MeHg.reference_method: Total-mercury screen; reflex MeHg speciation cannot exceed the tHg ceiling.

Al.control: No credible regulator sets an aluminium contaminant ML for seaweed. Seaweed accumulates aluminium from seawater/sediment as background; dietary aluminium is managed by weekly intake against the EFSA/JECFA TWI, not by a per-food maximum level.
Al.reference_method: Total-aluminium screen (ICP-MS); managed by intake vs the EFSA/JECFA TWI; no seaweed contaminant Al ML to align to.

Cr.control: No jurisdiction sets a total-chromium maximum level for seaweed or edible algae (the HK Cap 132V total-Cr limits are animal-seafood scope; the China GB 2762 total-Cr limits are cereals/beans plant scope — neither is on-scope for a marine macroalga). Chromium(III) is an essential nutrient; trace chromium in seaweed is geologic uptake. Screened as the substrate for reflex Cr-VI speciation.
Cr.reference_method: Total-chromium screen (ICP-MS); substrate for reflex Cr-VI speciation; no on-scope sovereign seaweed total-Cr ML.

Cr-VI.control: Cr-VI is bounded by the total-chromium screen (Cr-VI <= total Cr); no jurisdiction sets a Cr-VI food ML and there is no chromate pathway in seaweed (no lead-chromate adulteration as in spices), so any trace chromium is geologic chromium(III). Rebuttable if a routed source reports hexavalent chromium in seaweed.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Bounded by the total-chromium screen; reflex Cr-VI speciation only on anomalously elevated total chromium.
